chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) that Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Ziyad ibn Marwan al-Qandi, from Abu Waki', from Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, from al-Harith, who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Attend to sheep and agriculture, for they bring forth good in the evening and in the morning.
It was said: O Messenger of God, then what about camels?
He said: Those are the reins of the devils, and their benefit comes to us from the left (unlucky) side.
It was said: O Messenger of God, if people hear this, they will abandon them.
He said: Then the wicked sinners will not be deprived of them.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of camels being called the 'reins of the devils' in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith to highlight the economic wisdom behind the Prophet's preference for sheep and agriculture, which offer consistent daily returns, over the volatile nature of camel herding. The description of camels as the 'reins of the devils' and their benefits coming from the 'left side' (a sign of auspiciousness in Arab tradition) suggests a divine irony where the general public, fearing the 'evil eye' or misfortune, may abandon them, leaving them for the 'wicked and sinful' who are less affected by such superstitions. This reflects a Shia scholarly emphasis on practical wisdom and the socio-economic dynamics of early Muslim communities.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 2-44 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Yaqoob ibn Yazid, on the authority of Zyad ibn Marvan al-Qandi, on the authority of Abi Vaki’a, on the authority of Abi Ishaq al-Sabi’e, on the authority of Al-Harith, on the authority of the Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali (MGB) that God’s Prophet (MGB) said,
“I advise you to attend to agriculture and raising sheep, since these would provide you with benefits every dawn and dusk.”
The people asked the Prophet (MGB), “O Prophet of God! Then what about raising camels?”
The Prophet (MGB) replied, “Camels are the associates of Satan! Their benefits come to us in dangerous ways.”
The people said, “O Prophet of God! If the people hear this, they will abandon raising camels.”
The Prophet (MGB) replied, “No. The wicked ones will not!”
